synopsis: Samples colors anywhere on the screen with a touch-friendly floating picker
p_languages: The README is available in the following languages
p_introduction: 3-Color Picker is a local color sampling tool designed for touchscreens. Its floating picker pairs a draggable target ring with a live magnifier that shows a magnified pixel grid, the current color, and exact coordinates while keeping finger interaction direct and clear.
p_dual_mode: The same APK can run independently from the launcher or be discovered by AutoJs6 as the third extended tool in its drawer. Standalone mode does not require AutoJs6.
features: Two entry points: use it independently from the launcher or as an AutoJs6 extended tool
Touch optimized: drag the target ring for coarse moves and slide on the magnifier to fine-tune
Live readout: the magnifier shows the sampled color and its coordinates in real time
Flexible copy: copy the color as HEX or RGB, with an optional numeric-only form, or copy the coordinates
Controlled lifecycle: stop from the home screen, floating UI, notification, or host tool switch
Fully offline: screen content is never uploaded and screenshot history is not retained
standalone_steps: Open 3-Color Picker from the system launcher.
Tap Start color picker and follow the explanation to allow display over other apps.
Allow the current screen capture in the Android system prompt.
Switch to the app you want to sample, drag the target ring to the desired pixel, then slide on the magnifier disc to fine-tune.
Tap the color or coordinate text on the magnifier to copy it, long-press the color text to switch formats, or stop the picker at any time.
p_host: After installation AutoJs6 discovers the app through the formal plugin contract and shows its drawer tool only while the plugin is enabled in Plugin Center
host_steps: Install the plugin APK. You do not need to open its launcher entry first.
Open AutoJs6 Plugin Center and make sure 3-Color Picker is enabled. Authorize the plugin if prompted.
Open the AutoJs6 drawer. Screen Color Picker appears as the third Extended tools entry, with its runtime switch off by default.
Complete overlay and screen capture consent on first use.
Turn off the drawer switch, use the floating UI, or use the notification action to stop.
Disabling the plugin in Plugin Center hides the drawer entry. Re-enable the plugin to restore it.
p_privacy: All screen processing happens locally on the device and starts only after an explicit user action.
privacy_points: Screen capture: Android presents a system consent screen for each capture session
Display over other apps: used only for the touchable floating picker
Foreground service and notification: keep an active capture visible and stoppable
Clipboard: written only when the user taps a copy action
Network and storage: neither network nor shared storage permission is requested
p_permission_note: Denying the overlay or screen capture permission safely cancels startup. Denying notifications shows a warning and startup continues.
p_compatibility: Standalone and plugin modes have different minimum requirements.
p_contract: The following details are for host and plugin developers. The Binder service and Wake Activity are protected by org.autojs.permission.PLUGIN, while the launcher entry is not gated by that permission.
p_build: Use the checked-in Gradle Wrapper and JDK 21 to run tests, build the debug and instrumentation APKs, and then run lint.
p_docs_generation: README files, plugin instructions, and changelogs are generated from JSON copy sources. After editing a source, run both commands below.

Android installs it as a separate app; the old app can remain installed and settings are not migrated automatically. Grant permissions again and use AutoJs6 versionCode 5316 or later for host integration. The AutoJs6 drawer label remains Screen color picker.
instruction_p_what: 3-Color Picker is a screen color picker: a draggable target ring and a live magnifier select any pixel on the screen, and its color and coordinates can then be copied as HEX or RGB. It works on its own from the launcher, or as the "Screen color picker" tool in the AutoJs6 side drawer; the screen content is processed only on the device.
instruction_start_steps: Open 3-Color Picker from the launcher and tap "Start color picker".
When prompted, allow it to display over other apps, then allow this screen capture.
Switch to the app to sample, drag the target ring near the pixel, then slide on the magnifier disc to fine-tune.
Tap the color or coordinate text on the ring to copy it; tap the × at the bottom of the ring to stop.
instruction_features: **Floating picker**: The target ring covers long distances, while the magnifier shows the enlarged pixel grid, the current color and the coordinates; slide on the magnifier disc to move one pixel at a time.

**Copying colors and coordinates**: Tap the color or the coordinates to copy them, and long-press the color to switch between HEX and RGB; with "Copy numeric value only" on, the # and the R, G, B letters are left out.

**AutoJs6 side drawer**: Once the plugin is enabled in AutoJs6 "Plugin Center", the side drawer shows a "Screen color picker" switch that starts the picker when turned on and stops it when turned off.
**Picker settings**: Under "Picker settings" in "Settings", adjust "Magnifier size", "Sampling range", "Fine-tune speed" and "Show grid lines".
**Appearance**: "Language", "Dark mode" and "Theme color" default to "Follow AutoJs6" and can also be set separately; "Launcher icon" offers several styles.
**Running notification**: While the picker runs, the notification "Screen color picker is active" is shown with a "Stop" action.
**Release history and acknowledgements**: "Settings" also opens the "Release history" and the "Design reference and acknowledgements".
instruction_requirements: Android {{ min_android_version }} or later. Using it in the AutoJs6 side drawer requires AutoJs6 {{ required_host_version_name }} or later; using it on its own does not require AutoJs6.
The permission to display over other apps is used for the floating picker; Android asks you to confirm the screen capture each time the picker starts.
The notification permission is used for the running status and the "Stop" action; the picker still runs without it.
It does not use the network or save screenshots, and writes to the clipboard only when you tap to copy.

instruction_faq.q: When displaying over other apps or screen capture is denied
instruction_faq.a: The start is cancelled safely and no overlay is left behind. Tap "Start color picker" again to request the permission again.

instruction_faq.q: Why "Screen color picker" is missing from the AutoJs6 side drawer
instruction_faq.a: Make sure the plugin is enabled in AutoJs6 "Plugin Center", and authorize it if prompted. When the plugin is disabled in Plugin Center, the entry is hidden.
